papers.version_note: A web listing page of Quantum Computing Inc, not a paper: it holds titles, abstract excerpts, links, authors and years of about 36 publications and patents on thin-film lithium niobate devices. The text layer is one line with no page breaks, so it counts as one page.
papers.what_it_is: A vendor web page listing publications and patents from the Huang group on thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) photonic devices, with abstract excerpts.

assertions.value: The listing reports that a chip-integrated quasi-phase-matched lithium niobate microring resonator reaches a normalized frequency conversion efficiency of 230,000%/W.
assertions.anchor: Ultra-efficient frequency conversion in quasi-phase-matched lithium niobate microrings, listing entry
quotes: We demonstrate quasi-phase-matched frequency conversion in a chip-integrated lithium niobate microring resonator, whose normalized efficiency reaches 230,000%/W
assertions.certainty_reason: An abstract excerpt on a vendor page; the underlying paper was not read here.

assertions.value: The listing reports photon-pair generation in a periodically poled lithium niobate microresonator on chip at 8.5 and 36.3 MHz using 3.4 and 13.4 microwatt pump power, with a coincidence to accidental ratio above 100 at those rates.
assertions.anchor: Ultrabright Quantum Photon Sources on Chip, listing entry
quotes: we demonstrate photon-pair generation at high rates of 8.5 and 36.3 MHz using only 3.4 and 13.4 μ W pump power, respectively
The measured coincidence to accidental ratio is well above 100 at those high rates
assertions.certainty_reason: An abstract excerpt on a vendor page; the underlying paper was not read here.

assertions.value: The listing reports heralded single-photon generation at tens of megahertz rates from the same chip, with autocorrelation g H (2)(0) of 0.008 and 0.097 for the microwatt pumps.
assertions.anchor: Ultrabright Quantum Photon Sources on Chip, listing entry
quotes: The same chip enables heralded single-photon generation at tens of megahertz rates, each with low autocorrelation g H (2)(0)= 0.008 and 0.097 for the microwatt pumps
assertions.certainty_reason: An abstract excerpt on a vendor page; the underlying paper was not read here.

assertions.value: The listing reports a periodically poled lithium niobate nanowaveguide of 4 mm length with second harmonic generation efficiency over 2200% per watt per square centimeter (the exponents are printed flat in the text layer) and broadband difference frequency generation over a 4.3-THz span, with a coincidence to accidental ratio as high as 600.
assertions.anchor: Efficient parametric frequency conversion in lithium niobate nanophotonic chips, listing entry
quotes: Using a 4-mm nanowaveguide with subwavelength mode confinement, we demonstrate second harmonic generation with efficiency over 2200% W
broadband difference frequency generation over a 4.3-THz spectral span
with a coincidence to accidental ratio as high as 600
assertions.certainty_reason: An abstract excerpt on a vendor page; the underlying paper was not read here.
assertions.reader_inference: The text layer prints the unit exponents flat, so the exact unit is not quoted.

assertions.value: The listing reports a cascaded Mach-Zehnder design on lithium niobate thin film with up to 53 dB modulation extinction for wavelengths between 1500 nm and 1600 nm, against a stated limit of under 30 dB for current modulators.
assertions.anchor: High-extinction electro-optic modulation on lithium niobate thin film, listing entry
quotes: which currently suffers limited extinction (<30 dB) due to inevitable fabrication errors
demonstrating up to 53 dB modulation extinction for a wide range of wavelengths between 1500 nm and 1600 nm
assertions.certainty_reason: An abstract excerpt on a vendor page; the underlying paper was not read here.

assertions.value: The listing reports a dual-capacitor electrode layout with a voltage-length product of 0.64V cm for thin-film lithium niobate modulation, and lists a separate erratum stating that the results were corrected because of a wrong impedance setting of the arbitrary waveform generator.
assertions.anchor: Efficient electro-optical modulation on thin-film lithium niobate, and its erratum, listing entries
quotes: exceptional voltage–length product of 0.64V⋅cm
we correct the corresponding results of our Letter
due to the wrong impedance setting of the arbitrary waveform generator (AWG)
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract excerpts on a vendor page; the 0.64 figure is the original value that the listed erratum says was corrected, and the corrected value is not on this page.
assertions.reader_inference: The 0.64V cm figure should not be used without the corrected value from the erratum.

assertions.value: The listing reports sum-frequency generation on a periodically poled lithium niobate microring with external quantum efficiency (65±3)% at (104±4) microwatt pump power, a conversion probability of 10^-5 per single pump photon and a photon-photon coupling strength of 9.1 MHz.
assertions.anchor: Photon Conversion and Interaction in a Quasi-Phase-Matched Microresonator, listing entry
quotes: The external quantum efficiency reaches (65±3)% with only (104±4)-μ W pump power
we directly measure the conversion probability produced by a single pump photon to be 10− 5
the photon-photon coupling strength to be 9.1 MHz
assertions.certainty_reason: An abstract excerpt on a vendor page; the underlying paper was not read here.

assertions.value: The listing reports a noise level on the order of 10^-4 photons per time-frequency mode for high conversion in thin-film lithium niobate nanowaveguides, for telecom to near-visible conversion.

quotes: Our results find the noise level to be on the order of 10^−4 photons per time-frequency mode for high conversion

assertions.value: The listing reports observation of quantum Zeno blockade on chip, where a lightwave is modulated by another in an interaction-free manner, in a lithium niobate microdisk cavity, with an earlier whispering-gallery-mode resonator result of 80% modulation contrast at 100 microwatt pump peak power.
assertions.anchor: Observation of quantum zeno blockade on chip; On-Chip Demonstration of Interaction-free Quantum Switching; Observation of Quantum Zeno Blockade in χ (2) Microresonators, listing entries
quotes: we report on the observation of quantum Zeno blockade on chip, where a lightwave is modulated by another in a distinct "interaction-free" manner
Using a lithium-niobate microdisk cavity nanofabricated on chip
all-optical modulation with a contrast of 80% via quantum Zeno blockade in a Lithium Niobate whispering-gallery-mode resonator at a pump peak power of 100μW
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract excerpts on a vendor page; the underlying papers were not read here.

assertions.value: The listing describes a patent for a chip-integrated device that generates random numbers from quantum stochastic processes in optical parametric nonlinear media, with dimensionality varied from 2 to over 100,000 and real-time reconfiguration such as at 10 GHz speed.
assertions.anchor: Chip-integrated device and methods for generating random numbers (US11442697B2), listing entry
quotes: uses quantum stochastic processes in optical parametric nonlinear media
The dimensionality of the random numbers is varied from 2 to over 100,000
which are updated or reconfigured in real time, such as at 10 GHz speed
assertions.certainty_reason: A patent abstract excerpt on a vendor page, describing a device design.

assertions.value: The listing reports photon-pair generation in a heterogeneous hydrogenated amorphous silicon and silicon nitride chip with a coincidence-to-accidental ratio of 1632.6 (±260.4) at a pair generation rate of 1.94 MHz, and lowest heralded g H (2) (0) of 0.1085.
assertions.anchor: Photon-Pair Generation in a Heterogeneous Nanophotonic Chip, listing entry (2023)
quotes: A record high coincidence-to-accidental ratio value of 1632.6 (±260.4) is achieved in this heterogeneous design with a photon pair generation rate of 1.94 MHz
heralded single-photons with the lowest g H (2) (0) of 0.1085
assertions.certainty_reason: An abstract excerpt on a vendor page; the underlying paper was not read here. The platform is silicon, not lithium niobate.

assertions.value: The listing reports two remote-sensing uses of lithium niobate nanophotonic chips: an oxygen A-band absorption measurement near 770 nm with a micro-ring filter of 10 pm resonant linewidth and 25 dB extinction ratio, and a carbon dioxide absorption spectrum around 1572.022 nm using photon counting and a sweeping high-Q microring.

absorption line-shapes around 770 nm
